ESV.1: Now Solomon purposed to build a temple for the name of the LORD, and a royal palace for himself.
ESV.2: And Solomon assigned 70,000 men to bear burdens and 80,000 to quarry in the hill country, and 3,600 to oversee them.
ESV.3: And Solomon sent word to Hiram the king of Tyre: “As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedar to build himself a house to dwell in, so deal with me.
ESV.4: Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God and dedicate it to him for the burning of incense of sweet spices before him, and for the regular arrangement of the showbread, and for burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths and the new moons and the appointed feasts of the LORD our God, as ordained forever for Israel.
ESV.5: The house that I am to build will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
ESV.6: But who is able to build him a house, since heaven, even highest heaven, cannot contain him? Who am I to build a house for him, except as a place to make offerings before him?
ESV.7: So now send me a man skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue fabrics, trained also in engraving, to be with the skilled workers who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
ESV.8: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. And my servants will be with your servants,
ESV.9: to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the house I am to build will be great and wonderful.
ESV.10: I will give for your servants, the woodsmen who cut timber, 20,000 cors  of crushed wheat, 20,000 cors of barley, 20,000 baths  of wine, and 20,000 baths of oil.”
ESV.11: Then Hiram the king of Tyre answered in a letter that he sent to Solomon, “Because the LORD loves his people, he has made you king over them.”
ESV.12: Hiram also said, “Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, who has discretion and understanding, who will build a temple for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
ESV.13: “Now I have sent a skilled man, who has understanding, Huram-abi,
ESV.14: the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre. He is trained to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, and in purple, blue, and crimson fabrics and fine linen, and to do all sorts of engraving and execute any design that may be assigned him, with your craftsmen, the craftsmen of my lord, David your father.
ESV.15: Now therefore the wheat and barley, oil and wine, of which my lord has spoken, let him send to his servants.
ESV.16: And we will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa, so that you may take it up to Jerusalem.”
ESV.17: Then Solomon counted all the resident aliens who were in the land of Israel, after the census of them that David his father had taken, and there were found 153,600.
ESV.18: Seventy thousand of them he assigned to bear burdens, 80,000 to quarry in the hill country, and 3,600 as overseers to make the people work.

NKJV.1: Then Solomon determined to build a temple for the name of the LORD, and a royal house for himself.
NKJV.2: Solomon selected seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand to quarry stone in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
NKJV.3: Then Solomon sent to Hiram king of Tyre, saying: As you have dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build himself a house to dwell in, so deal with me.
NKJV.4: Behold, I am building a temple for the name of the LORD my God, to dedicate it to Him, to burn before Him sweet incense, for the continual showbread, for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, on the New Moons, and on the set feasts of the LORD our God. This is an ordinance forever to Israel.
NKJV.5: And the temple which I build will be great, for our God is greater than all gods.
NKJV.6: But who is able to build Him a temple, since heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain Him? Who am I then, that I should build Him a temple, except to burn sacrifice before Him?
NKJV.7: Therefore send me at once a man skillful to work in gold and silver, in bronze and iron, in purple and crimson and blue, who has skill to engrave with the skillful men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
NKJV.8: Also send me cedar and cypress and algum logs from Lebanon, for I know that your servants have skill to cut timber in Lebanon; and indeed my servants will be with your servants,
NKJV.9: to prepare timber for me in abundance, for the temple which I am about to build shall be great and wonderful.
NKJV.10: And indeed I will give to your servants, the woodsmen who cut timber, twenty thousand kors of ground wheat, twenty thousand kors of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.
NKJV.11: Then Hiram king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon:  Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them.
NKJV.12: Hiram also said: Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, for He has given King David a wise son, endowed with prudence and understanding, who will build a temple for the LORD and a royal house for himself!
NKJV.13: And now I have sent a skillful man, endowed with understanding, Huram my master craftsman
NKJV.14: (the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan, and his father was a man of Tyre), skilled to work in gold and silver, bronze and iron, stone and wood, purple and blue, fine linen and crimson, and to make any engraving and to accomplish any plan which may be given to him, with your skillful men and with the skillful men of my lord David your father.
NKJV.15: Now therefore, the wheat, the barley, the oil, and the wine which my lord has spoken of, let him send to his servants.
NKJV.16: And we will cut wood from Lebanon, as much as you need; we will bring it to you in rafts by sea to Joppa, and you will carry it up to Jerusalem.
NKJV.17: Then Solomon numbered all the aliens who were in the land of Israel, after the census in which David his father had numbered them; and there were found to be one hundred and fifty-three thousand six hundred.
NKJV.18: And he made seventy thousand of them bearers of burdens, eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountain, and three thousand six hundred overseers to make the people work.

NASB.1: Now Solomon decided to build a house for the name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
NASB.2: So Solomon assigned 70,000 men to carry loads and 80,000 men to quarry [stone] in the mountains and 3,600 to supervise them.
NASB.3: Then Solomon sent [word] to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, 'As you dealt with David my father and sent him cedars to build him a house to dwell in, so do for me.
NASB.4: 'Behold, I am about to build a house for the name of the LORD my God, dedicating it to Him, to burn fragrant incense before Him and [to set out] the showbread continually, and to offer burnt offerings morning and evening, on sabbaths and on new moons and on the appointed feasts of the LORD our God, this [being required] forever in Israel.
NASB.5: 'The house which I am about to build [will be] great, for greater is our God than all the gods.
NASB.6: 'But who is able to build a house for Him, for the heavens and the highest heavens cannot contain Him? So who am I, that I should build a house for Him, except to burn [incense] before Him?
NASB.7: 'Now send me a skilled man to work in gold, silver, brass and iron, and in purple, crimson and violet [fabrics], and who knows how to make engravings, to [work] with the skilled men whom I have in Judah and Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
NASB.8: 'Send me also cedar, cypress and algum timber from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber of Lebanon; and indeed my servants [will work] with your servants,
NASB.9: to prepare timber in abundance for me, for the house which I am about to build [will be] great and wonderful.
NASB.10: 'Now behold, I will give to your servants, the woodsmen who cut the timber, 20,000 kors of crushed wheat and 20,000 kors of barley, and 20,000 baths of wine and 20,000 baths of oil.'
NASB.11: Then Huram, king of Tyre, answered in a letter sent to Solomon: 'Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them.'
NASB.12: Then Huram continued, 'Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
NASB.13: 'Now I am sending Huram-abi, a skilled man, endowed with understanding,
NASB.14: the son of a Danite woman and a Tyrian father, who knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone and wood, [and] in purple, violet, linen and crimson fabrics, and [who knows how] to make all kinds of engravings and to execute any design which may be assigned to him, [to work] with your skilled men and with those of my lord David your father.
NASB.15: 'Now then, let my lord send to his servants wheat and barley, oil and wine, of which he has spoken.
NASB.16: 'We will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you on rafts by sea to Joppa, so that you may carry it up to Jerusalem.'
NASB.17: Solomon numbered all the aliens who [were] in the land of Israel, following the census which his father David had taken; and 153,600 were found.
NASB.18: He appointed 70,000 of them to carry loads and 80,000 to quarry [stones] in the mountains and 3,600 supervisors to make the people work.

NLT.1: Solomon decided to build a Temple to honor the name of the LORD, and also a royal palace for himself.
NLT.2: He enlisted a force of 70,000 laborers, 80,000 men to quarry stone in the hill country, and 3,600 foremen.
NLT.3: Solomon also sent this message to King Hiram at Tyre: “Send me cedar logs as you did for my father, David, when he was building his palace.
NLT.4: I am about to build a Temple to honor the name of the LORD my God. It will be a place set apart to burn fragrant incense before him, to display the special sacrificial bread, and to sacrifice burnt offerings each morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, at new moon celebrations, and at the other appointed festivals of the LORD our God. He has commanded Israel to do these things forever.
NLT.5: “This must be a magnificent Temple because our God is greater than all other gods.
NLT.6: But who can really build him a worthy home? Not even the highest heavens can contain him! So who am I to consider building a Temple for him, except as a place to burn sacrifices to him?
NLT.7: “So send me a master craftsman who can work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, as well as with purple, scarlet, and blue cloth. He must be a skilled engraver who can work with the craftsmen of Judah and Jerusalem who were selected by my father, David.
NLT.8: “Also send me cedar, cypress, and red sandalwood logs from Lebanon, for I know that your men are without equal at cutting timber in Lebanon. I will send my men to help them.
NLT.9: An immense amount of timber will be needed, for the Temple I am going to build will be very large and magnificent.
NLT.10: In payment for your woodcutters, I will send 100,000 bushels of crushed wheat, 100,000 bushels of barley, 110,000 gallons of wine, and 110,000 gallons of olive oil. ”
NLT.11: King Hiram sent this letter of reply to Solomon: “It is because the LORD loves his people that he has made you their king!
NLT.12: Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth! He has given King David a wise son, gifted with skill and understanding, who will build a Temple for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
NLT.13: “I am sending you a master craftsman named Huram-abi, who is extremely talented.
NLT.14: His mother is from the tribe of Dan in Israel, and his father is from Tyre. He is skillful at making things from gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and he also works with stone and wood. He can work with purple, blue, and scarlet cloth and fine linen. He is also an engraver and can follow any design given to him. He will work with your craftsmen and those appointed by my lord David, your father.
NLT.15: “Send along the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine that my lord has mentioned.
NLT.16: We will cut whatever timber you need from the Lebanon mountains and will float the logs in rafts down the coast of the Mediterranean Sea to Joppa. From there you can transport the logs up to Jerusalem.”
NLT.17: Solomon took a census of all foreigners in the land of Israel, like the census his father had taken, and he counted 153,600.
NLT.18: He assigned 70,000 of them as common laborers, 80,000 as quarry workers in the hill country, and 3,600 as foremen.

WEB.1: Now Solomon decided to build a house for Yahweh’s name, and a house for his kingdom.
WEB.2: Solomon counted out seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
WEB.3: Solomon sent to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, “As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build him a house in which to dwell, so deal with me.
WEB.4: Behold,  I am about to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God, to dedicate it to him, to burn before him incense of sweet spices, for the continual show bread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts of Yahweh our God. This is an ordinance forever to Israel.
WEB.5: “The house which I am building will be great; for our God is greater than all gods.
WEB.6: But who is able to build him a house, since heaven and the heaven of heavens can’t contain him? Who am I then, that I should build him a house, except just to burn incense before him?
WEB.7: “Now therefore send me a man skillful to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue, and who knows how to engrave engravings, to be with the skillful men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.
WEB.8: “Send me also cedar trees, cypress trees, and algum trees out of Lebanon; for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. Behold, my servants will be with your servants,
WEB.9: even to prepare me timber in abundance; for the house which I am about to build will be great and wonderful.
WEB.10: Behold, I will give to your servants, the cutters who cut timber, twenty thousand cors  of beaten wheat, twenty thousand baths  of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
WEB.11: Then Huram the king of Tyre answered in writing, which he sent to Solomon, “Because Yahweh loves his people, he has made you king over them.”
WEB.12: Huram continued, “Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who would build a house for Yahweh, and a house for his kingdom.
WEB.13: Now I have sent a skillful man, endowed with understanding, of Huram my father’s,
WEB.14: the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan; and his father was a man of Tyre, skillful to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, in timber, and in purple, in blue, in fine linen, and in crimson, also to engrave any kind of engraving and to devise any device; that there may be a place appointed to him with your skillful men, and with the skillful men of my lord David your father.
WEB.15: “Now therefore the wheat the barley, the oil and the wine, which my lord has spoken of, let him send to his servants;
WEB.16: and we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as you need. We will bring it to you in floats by sea to Joppa; and you shall carry it up to Jerusalem.”
WEB.17: Solomon counted all the foreigners who were in the land of Israel, after the census with which David his father had counted them; and they found one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred.
WEB.18: He set seventy thousand of them to bear burdens, eighty thousand who were stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers to assign the people their work.

CSB17.1: Solomon decided to build a temple for the name of the LORD and a royal palace for himself, <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.2: so he assigned 70,000 men as porters, 80,000 men as stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 as supervisors over them. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.3: Then Solomon sent word to King Hiram <sup>[1]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup> of Tyre: <sup>ⓜ</sup> Do for me what you did for my father David. You sent him cedars to build him a house to live in. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.4: Now I am building a temple for the name of the LORD my God in order to dedicate it to him for burning fragrant incense before him, <sup>ⓐ</sup> for displaying the rows of the Bread of the Presence continuously, <sup>ⓑ</sup> and for sacrificing burnt offerings for the morning and the evening, <sup>ⓒ</sup> the Sabbaths <sup>ⓓ</sup> and the New Moons, and the appointed festivals of the LORD our God. This is ordained for Israel permanently.
CSB17.5: The temple that I am building will be great, for our God is greater than any of the gods. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.6: But who is able to build a temple for him, since even heaven and the highest heaven cannot contain him? <sup>ⓕ</sup> Who am I then that I should build a temple for him except as a place to burn incense before him?
CSB17.7: Therefore, send me an artisan who is skilled in engraving to work with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and with purple, crimson, and blue yarn. He will work with the artisans who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, <sup>ⓖ</sup> appointed by my father David. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.8: Also, send me cedar, cypress, and algum <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓘ</sup> logs from Lebanon, for I know that your servants know how to cut the trees of Lebanon. Note that my servants will be with your servants <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.9: to prepare logs for me in abundance because the temple I am building will be great and wondrous.
CSB17.10: I will give your servants, the woodcutters who cut the trees, one hundred thousand bushels <sup>[3]</sup> of wheat flour, one hundred thousand bushels of barley, one hundred ten thousand gallons <sup>[4]</sup> of wine, and one hundred ten thousand gallons of oil.
CSB17.11: Then King Hiram of Tyre wrote a letter <sup>[5]</sup> and sent it to Solomon: Because the LORD loves his people, he set you over them as king. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.12: Hiram also said: Blessed be the LORD God of Israel, who made the heavens and the earth! <sup>ⓛ</sup> He gave King David a wise son with insight and understanding, <sup>ⓜ</sup> who will build a temple for the LORD and a royal palace for himself. <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.13: I have now sent Huram-abi, <sup>[6]</sup> a skillful man who has understanding. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.14: He is the son of a woman from the daughters of Dan. His father is a man of Tyre. He knows how to work with gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, with purple, blue, crimson yarn, and fine linen. He knows how to do all kinds of engraving and to execute any design that may be given him. I have sent him to be with your artisans and the artisans of my lord, your father David.
CSB17.15: Now, let my lord send the wheat, barley, oil, and wine to his servants as promised. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.16: We will cut logs from Lebanon, as many as you need, and bring them to you as rafts by sea to Joppa. You can then take them up to Jerusalem. <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.17: Solomon took a census of all the resident alien men in the land of Israel, after the census that his father David had conducted, <sup>ⓓ</sup> and the total was 153,600.
CSB17.18: Solomon made 70,000 of them porters, 80,000 stonecutters in the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors to make the people work. <sup>ⓔ</sup>

AMP.1: Now Solomon decided to build a house (temple) for the Name of the LORD, and a royal palace for himself.
AMP.2: So Solomon assigned 70,000 men to carry loads, 80,000 men to quarry stone in the mountains, and 3,600 to supervise them.
AMP.3: Then Solomon sent word to Hiram king of Tyre, saying, "As you dealt with my father David and sent him cedars to build himself a house in which to live, [please] do the same for me.
AMP.4: Observe, I am about to build a house for the Name of the LORD my God, dedicated to Him, to burn fragrant incense [of sweet spices] before Him, to set out the showbread continually, and to offer burnt offerings morning and evening, on Sabbaths, New Moons, and on the festivals of the LORD our God, as ordained forever in Israel.
AMP.5: The house I am going to build will be great, for our God is greater than all the gods.
AMP.6: But who is able to build a house for Him, since the heavens and [even] the highest heavens cannot contain Him? Who am I to build a house for Him, except [as a place] to burn incense before Him?
AMP.7: Now send me a man who is skilled to work in gold, silver, bronze, and iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue fabrics, and who knows how to make engravings, to work with the skilled men who are with me in Judah and Jerusalem, whom my father David provided.
AMP.8: Send me also cedar, cypress, and algum timber, for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. And indeed my servants will work with your servants
AMP.9: to prepare for me an abundance of timber, because the house I am about to build will be great and wonderful.
AMP.10: And I will give to your servants who cut timber, 20,000 measures of crushed wheat and 20,000 measures of barley, and 20,000 baths of wine and 20,000 baths of [olive] oil."
AMP.11: Then Hiram, king of Tyre replied in a letter sent to Solomon: "Because the LORD loves His people, He has made you king over them."
AMP.12: Hiram said also, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given King David a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who will build a house for the LORD and a royal palace for himself.
AMP.13: "Now I am sending a skilled man, endowed with understanding, Huram-abi,
AMP.14: the son of a Danite woman and a Tyrian father. He is trained to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood; in purple, blue, and crimson fabrics, and in fine linen. He is able to make any kind of engraving and to carry out any design given him. He will work with your skilled men and those of my lord, David your father.
AMP.15: Now then, let my lord send to his servants the wheat, the barley, the oil, and the wine of which he has spoken.
AMP.16: We will cut whatever timber you need from Lebanon and bring it to you on rafts by sea to Joppa, so that you may take it up to Jerusalem."
AMP.17: Then Solomon took a count of all the aliens in the land of Israel, like the census that his father David had taken; and they were found to be 153,600.
AMP.18: He assigned 70,000 of them to carry loads and 80,000 to quarry stone in the mountain, and 3,600 as overseers to make the people work.

MSG.1: Solomon gave orders to begin construction on the house of worship in honor of God and a palace for himself.
MSG.2: Solomon assigned 70,000 common laborers, 80,000 to work the quarries in the mountains, and 3,600 foremen to manage the workforce.
MSG.3: Then Solomon sent this message to King Hiram of Tyre: "Send me cedar logs, the same kind you sent David my father for building his palace.
MSG.4: I'm about to build a house of worship in honor of God, a holy place for burning perfumed incense, for setting out holy bread, for making Whole-Burnt-Offerings at morning and evening worship, and for Sabbath, New Moon, and Holy Day services of worship—the acts of worship required of Israel.
MSG.5: "The house I am building has to be the best, for our God is the best, far better than competing gods.
MSG.6: But who is capable of building such a structure? Why, the skies—the entire cosmos!—can't begin to contain him. And me, who am I to think I can build a house adequate for God—burning incense to him is about all I'm good for!
MSG.7: I need your help: Send me a master artisan in gold, silver, bronze, iron, textiles of purple, crimson, and violet, and who knows the craft of engraving; he will supervise the trained craftsmen in Judah and Jerusalem that my father provided.
MSG.8: Also send cedar, cypress, and algum logs from Lebanon; I know you have lumberjacks experienced in the Lebanon forests. I'll send workers to join your crews
MSG.9: to cut plenty of timber—I'm going to need a lot, for this house I'm building is going to be absolutely stunning—a showcase temple!
MSG.10: I'll provide all the food necessary for your crew of lumberjacks and loggers: 130,000 bushels of wheat, 120,000 gallons of wine, and 120,000 gallons of olive oil."
MSG.11: Hiram king of Tyre wrote Solomon in reply: "It's plain that God loves his people—he made you king over them!"
MSG.12: He wrote on, "Blessed be the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, and who gave King David a son so wise, so knowledgeable and shrewd, to build a temple for God and a palace for himself.
MSG.13: I've sent you Huram-Abi—he's already on his way—he knows the construction business inside and out.
MSG.14: His mother is from Dan and his father from Tyre. He knows how to work in gold, silver, bronze, iron, stone, and wood, in purple, violet, linen, and crimson textiles; he is also an expert engraver and competent to work out designs with your artists and architects, and those of my master David, your father.
MSG.15: "Go ahead and send the wheat, barley, olive oil, and wine you promised for my work crews.
MSG.16: We'll log the trees you need from the Lebanon forests and raft them down to Joppa. You'll have to get the timber up to Jerusalem yourself."
MSG.17: Solomon then took a census of all the foreigners living in Israel, using the same census-taking method employed by his father. They numbered 153,600.
MSG.18: He assigned 70,000 of them as common laborers, 80,000 to work the quarries in the mountains, and 3,600 as foremen to manage the work crews.
